title: Of Envy and Malice

full_text:
On the eighth day, the Eighth Wazir argued before King Azadbakht. Bakhtiyar stood before the throne and delivered his discourse on the destructive nature of envy:

'O King! Envy is the most venomous serpent that crawls within the human breast. The thief steals for hunger or gain, the angry man strikes for a perceived injury; but the envious man suffers agony simply because his neighbor prospers!

The envious man looks upon another’s happiness as his own personal calamity; the sun that warms the earth burns his eyes, and the rain that fertilizes the fields chokes his throat.

He does not seek to elevate his own condition through labor; he desires only to pull down the noble to his own mire. Yet look upon the end of all envious schemers: they consume their own flesh with bitter bile, while the righteous man continues to shine like the sun above the clouds.

Malice is a boomerang that returns with double force upon the hand that threw it, as the chronicle of King Aylan Shah and Abu Tammam demonstrates.'
moral: Envy consumes the heart of the envious man, destroying his own peace while leaving the good unharmed.
